A variable rate is tied to the Bank of Canada's policy rate. When that rate goes up, you pay more; when it goes down, you pay less. You can save, but you need to be comfortable with the idea that your payment may increase. The important point to remember: the real difference often doesn't show in the rate, but in the penalty if you break your loan before the end.
